statement: What is the remainder when 2 to the power 30 is divided by 7?

choices.misconception: I found the cycle 2, 4, 1 but read the remainder of 30 divided by 3 as one instead of zero.
I counted the cycle positions from zero, which shifted my answer one step along.
I divided 30 by 7 and used that remainder rather than the remainder of the powers.
I assumed the remainder would be one less than the divisor because the power is large.

hints: Work out the first few powers and their remainders.
Remainders of powers repeat on a short cycle. Find the remainders of 2, 4, 8, 16 and so on when divided by 7, and stop as soon as the list starts repeating.
The remainders go 2, 4, 1, then 2, 4, 1 again - a cycle of length 3. Since 30 is a multiple of 3, the answer is the last of the cycle, which is 1.

solutions.reliable: Build the cycle of remainders. 2 leaves 2, 4 leaves 4, 8 leaves 1, 16 leaves 2, 32 leaves 4, 64 leaves 1 - so the remainders repeat every 3 powers as 2, 4, 1. Because 30 divides exactly by 3, the thirtieth power sits at the end of a full cycle, giving remainder 1. The transferable idea: a remainder of zero lands on the last entry of the cycle, not the first.
solutions.elegant: 2 cubed is 8, which is one more than 7, so 2 to the power 30 is (2 cubed) to the power 10, which leaves the same remainder as 1 to the power 10 - namely 1.

whyOnTest: It is the remainder cycle again with a bigger modulus, and the remainder-of-zero edge case is exactly where students slip.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
